rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase (1.6% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027)
rules.requirement: If you live in a rent-controlled San Francisco unit, your landlord's annual rent increase from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 may not exceed 1.6% of your base rent. For example, a $2,000 base rent can rise by no more than $32.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units under the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. The members do not define coverage. The city's just-cause page (D079) says units that first got a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from the rent increase limits.
rules.exemptions: Per D079 (just-cause context): newly built units first certified for occupancy after June 13, 1979; tenancies where Costa-Hawkins allows rent increases; and some units whose rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.reason: Both official pages state the same 1.6% allowable increase under S.F. Admin. Code § 37.3(a)(1), so they were merged. The effective date is left null because 2026-03-01 is only an annual adjustment date and no member gives the ordinance's original effective date. The coverage cutoff comes from the just-cause context.
